detected.purpose: Intake the alert signal, create workflow context, and define the first investigation scope before deeper analysis begins.

whatToVerify.1: Confirm the alert source, matched rule, affected asset, user, and first seen time.
whatToVerify.2: Check whether the signal is a duplicate of an existing workflow or belongs to a related case.
whatToVerify.3: Capture the initial business impact so the analyst knows where to start.

completionCriteria.1: The workflow has a concrete asset, time window, and alert reason.
completionCriteria.2: The signal is not an obvious duplicate or already covered by another active case.
completionCriteria.3: The case has enough context for triage to start.

detected.riskNote: Do not escalate before the signal is tied to a concrete case, asset, or time window.
detected.recommendedReason: Once the signal has enough context, the next useful action is analyst triage.
detected.transitionEffect: Moving to Investigating records triage start and shifts the workbench toward evidence review.

investigating.purpose: Determine whether the alert represents real malicious activity or should be closed as benign or false positive.

whatToVerify.1: Review the AI report, trace graph, rule hits, and endpoint evidence together.
whatToVerify.2: Look for behavior that proves intent, execution, persistence, command activity, or lateral movement.
whatToVerify.3: Compare suspicious signals against known benign operations for the same host or user.

completionCriteria.1: Evidence is strong enough to confirm the attack or close it with a clear reason.
completionCriteria.2: Important trace nodes and supporting events have been reviewed.
completionCriteria.3: The analyst note explains the classification decision.

investigating.riskNote: Do not confirm without evidence that links the observed behavior to an attack path.
investigating.recommendedReason: When classification evidence is clear, the workflow should move from triage into a formal decision state.
investigating.transitionEffect: Moving forward records the investigation decision and enables confirmation, forensics, or closure handling.

confirmed.purpose: Record that the attack is verified, preserve the decision context, and prepare the case for evidence capture.

whatToVerify.1: Confirm the malicious behavior, affected assets, severity, and known attack path.
whatToVerify.2: Make sure the confirmation event references traceable evidence, not only a manual assertion.
whatToVerify.3: Check whether response urgency changes the amount of forensics that can be collected first.

completionCriteria.1: The attack classification is recorded and visible in the timeline.
completionCriteria.2: The main evidence supporting confirmation is available for review.
completionCriteria.3: The case is ready for forensics or an explicitly justified fast response path.

confirmed.riskNote: Avoid skipping evidence capture when response actions may destroy forensic context.
confirmed.recommendedReason: The attack has been verified, so the next step is to preserve evidence before response work changes the environment.
confirmed.transitionEffect: Moving to Forensics records the verification point and focuses the workbench on evidence capture.

forensics.purpose: Capture and preserve the evidence needed to explain what happened before execution-oriented response begins.

whatToVerify.1: Collect the timeline, process tree, artifacts, affected host details, and user context.
whatToVerify.2: Confirm whether volatile evidence must be captured before isolation or cleanup.
whatToVerify.3: Identify the evidence that response operators need to choose safe actions.

completionCriteria.1: Critical artifacts and timeline evidence are preserved or explicitly marked as unavailable.
completionCriteria.2: The response team has enough context to act without destroying required evidence.
completionCriteria.3: The next response action can be audited against collected evidence.

forensics.riskNote: Avoid destructive response before collecting the evidence needed for review, reporting, or root cause analysis.
forensics.recommendedReason: After evidence is preserved, the workflow can move into response preparation and execution.
forensics.transitionEffect: Moving to Responding opens the workflow for response action preview, execution, and result tracking.

responding.purpose: Prepare, preview, execute, and sync response actions while keeping the operator decision auditable.

whatToVerify.1: Review the action preview, execution target, expected impact, and rollback considerations.
whatToVerify.2: Confirm that response tasks are aimed at the correct host, process, account, or network path.
whatToVerify.3: Check execution results and synchronize task status back into the workflow timeline.

completionCriteria.1: Response actions have been executed, skipped with reason, or queued with visible status.
completionCriteria.2: The operator note explains the selected action path and known impact.
completionCriteria.3: The workflow has enough result data to validate containment.

responding.riskNote: Review targets carefully before actions that isolate hosts, terminate processes, or block accounts.
responding.recommendedReason: Once response actions are complete or ready to validate, the case should move to containment validation.
responding.transitionEffect: Moving to Contained records active response completion and starts validation that the attack path is stopped.

contained.purpose: Validate that the active attack path, spread channel, and control path are stopped before cleanup begins.

whatToVerify.1: Check isolation, block, termination, and access-control results against the affected scope.
whatToVerify.2: Look for remaining active connections, suspicious processes, callbacks, or lateral movement.
whatToVerify.3: Confirm monitoring signals show no continued execution inside the known attack path.

completionCriteria.1: Active spread and command paths are halted or explicitly accepted as residual risk.
completionCriteria.2: Containment evidence is recorded and visible in the timeline.
completionCriteria.3: Cleanup and recovery can start without allowing the active attack to continue.

contained.riskNote: Do not mark contained if active execution or lateral movement is still visible.
contained.recommendedReason: Validated containment means the team can move from stopping the attack to cleaning and recovering affected assets.
contained.transitionEffect: Moving to Remediated records containment completion and shifts the workbench to cleanup validation.

remediated.purpose: Verify cleanup, recovery, and prevention controls before the workflow is closed.

whatToVerify.1: Confirm malicious artifacts are removed and affected systems or policies are restored.
whatToVerify.2: Review validation scans, monitoring signals, or analyst checks for recurrence.
whatToVerify.3: Make sure the final close reason is supported by the remediation evidence.

completionCriteria.1: Cleanup is complete and no active recurrence is visible.
completionCriteria.2: Recovery and prevention tasks have a recorded result.
completionCriteria.3: The case has a clear closure reason and enough audit evidence for review.

remediated.riskNote: Do not close while recovery evidence, validation data, or the final close reason is missing.
remediated.recommendedReason: When cleanup is validated, the workflow can be closed with a final reason and audit trail.
remediated.transitionEffect: Moving to Closed records final resolution and locks the workflow into review mode.

closed.purpose: Keep the final decision, close reason, timeline, and operator notes available for audit and review.

whatToVerify.1: Review the close reason, final operator note, and last workflow event.
whatToVerify.2: Confirm the timeline explains how the case moved from detection to closure.
whatToVerify.3: Check whether any follow-up task should be tracked outside this closed workflow.

completionCriteria.1: Closure is recorded with a clear reason.
completionCriteria.2: No further workflow action is required inside this case.
completionCriteria.3: The audit trail is complete enough for later review.

closed.riskNote: Closed workflows should be reopened only through an explicit follow-up process.
closed.recommendedReason: Closed workflows are review-only and should not receive automatic stage transitions.
closed.transitionEffect: No transition is executed from Closed in this workbench.
